report:
Antecedentes Clínicos:
Condropatía patelar. Obs. Rotura meniscal lateral. Obs. Cuerpo libre.
Hallazgos:
Ligamentos cruzados y colaterales dentro de límites normales.
Fibrilación marginal del cuerno posterior del menisco medial. No se observan otras alteraciones
del menisco medial.
Menisco lateral de morfología y señal conservada, sin criterios de una rotura categórica.
Úlceras condrales de espesor parcial de la región central de la zona de carga del cóndilo femoral
medial. El resto de los cartílagos femorotibiales sin alteraciones significativas.
Úlceras condrales de espesor total con cambios óseos secundarios a la articulación patelofemoral
de predominio lateral y proliferaciones óseas periféricas.
Leve derrame articular con sinovitis difusa. Cuerpos intraarticulares en receso posterior de hasta 7
mm.
Leve aumento de señal de la inserción distal del tendón cuadricipital, sin signos de rotura. Discreto
edema el paquete adiposo retro cuadricipital suprarrotuliano de manera reactiva. Tendón rotuliano,
tendones de la pata de ganso, bíceps femoral y banda iliotibial dentro de límites normales.
Impresión:
Avanzados cambios degenerativos de la articulación patelofemoral de predominio lateral.
Fibrilación marginal del cuerno posterior del menisco medial.
Leve derrame articular con sinovitis difusa. Cuerpos intraarticulares en receso posterior.
Leve tendinosis cuadricipital distal con discreto edema el paquete adiposo retro cuadricipital
suprarrotuliano de manera reactiva

Exam Type: MRI KNEE LEFT WO CONTRAST
Exam Date and Time: [DATE] [TIME]
Indication: Left knee pain for 4 days.
Comparison: No relevant prior studies available for comparison.

TECHNIQUE:
MRI of the left knee was performed on a 1.2 Tesla open system with a dedicated knee coil in three planes (axial, sagittal, and coronal), using a standard non-contrast protocol.

FINDINGS:
OSSEOUS STRUCTURES:
Alignment is anatomic. No acute fracture. Normal background marrow signal. No focal osseous lesion.

JOINT SPACE:
Small joint effusion. Small multiloculated Baker's cyst.

MEDIAL COMPARTMENT:
Medial meniscus: Radial tear at the posterior root.
Medial compartment cartilage: Low-grade articular cartilage loss at the weightbearing aspect of the joint.

LATERAL COMPARTMENT:
Lateral meniscus: No tear.
Lateral compartment cartilage: Low-grade articular cartilage loss at the weightbearing aspect of the joint.

PATELLOFEMORAL COMPARTMENT:
Patellofemoral compartment cartilage: Low-grade articular cartilage loss at the patella.

CRUCIATE LIGAMENTS:
Anterior cruciate ligament (ACL): No tear.
Posterior cruciate ligament (PCL): No tear.

COLLATERAL LIGAMENTS & POSTEROLATERAL CORNER:
Medial collateral ligament (MCL): Normal.
Lateral collateral ligament (LCL) complex: Normal.
Posterolateral corner structures: Normal.

EXTENSOR MECHANISM:
Extensor Apparatus: Normal quadriceps tendon. Normal patellar tendon.
Medial patellofemoral ligament (MPFL) and patellar retinacula: Normal.
Patellofemoral tracking: Edema in superolateral Hoffa's fat pad. No lateral patellar tilt or translation. No patella alta. Shallow trochlear groove. Tibial tubercle-trochlear groove (TT-TG) distance is 4 mm, normal.

MUSCLES/TENDONS:
No disproportionate muscle atrophy. Visualized tendons not previously discussed are intact.

SOFT TISSUES:
Nonspecific prepatellar and scattered subcutaneous edema about the knee. No soft tissue mass. Normal popliteal neurovascular bundle.

IMPRESSION:

1.	Focal radial tear at the medial meniscus posterior root.
2.	Mild tricompartmental chondrosis. Small knee joint effusion with mild synovitis. Small multiloculated Baker's cyst.
3.	Superolateral Hoffa's fat pad impingement, suggesting lateral patellofemoral maltracking.

In den vorliegenden Sequenzen unauffällige Signalgebung der ossären Strukturen, kein bone bruise, kein Knochenmarksödem. Stigmata einer geringen, lateral betonten Gonarthrose mit kleinen osteophytären Anbauten an den Femurkondylen bds. Gering oberflächlich geminderter Knorpelbesatz im medialen sowie lateralen Kompartiment. Keine wesentliche Chondropathie retropatellar. V. a. kleinen radiären Riss im Hinterhorn des Innenmeniskus (3/103). Außenmeniskus ohne Anhalt für eine Rissbildung. Geringe mukoide, degenerative Signalalterationen des Innen- und Außenmeniskus. VKB und HKB intakt. MCL und LCL intakt. Akzentuierte Gelenkflüssigkeit. Intakte Signalgebung der Quadrizeps- sowie der Patellarsehne. Geringe Bursitis präpatellaris, ansonsten die miterfassten Weichteile in den vorliegenden Sequenzen mit unauffälliger Signalgebung.

SAĞ DİZ MRG. Tetkik protokolü: Çok düzlemli, çok sekanslı. Bulgular: Lateral menisküs anterior-posterior horn ve gövde kesiminde grade II dejenerasyon izlenmektedir. Medial menisküs posterior horn ve gövde kesiminde grade II dejenerasyon izlenmektedir. Ön çapraz bağ ve arka çapraz bağ, lateral kollateral ligaman normaldir. Medial kollateral ligamande periligamantöz ödem izlenmektedir. Distal kuadriseps ve patellar tendonlar normaldir. Patella normal yerleşimlidir. Retinaküler devamsızlık yoktur.Gastroknemius medial krus proksimali insersiyo düzeyinde tendinozis ile uyumlu sinyal değişikliği izlenmektedir.Suprapateller bursada sıvı artışı ve sinovyal kalınlaşma izlenmektedir. Tibiofemoral eklem mesafesinde sıvı artışı izlenmektedir. Tibia femoral eklem düzeyinde kemik yapı köşelerde milimetrik osteofitik sivrileşme izlenmektedir.Tibiofemoral eklem medialde eklem aralığında daralma, ekleme komşu femoral ve tibial kartilajlarda incelme izlenmektedir.Popliteal fossada 6x3 cm boyutlu Baker kisti izlenmektedir. Sonuç: Hafif düzeyde gonartroz,Medial ve lateral menisküslerde grade II meniskopati, Suprapateller bursit,Diz ekleminde hafif sinovit, Gastroknemius medial krus tendinozisi,Popliteal fossada baker kisti, Medial kollateral ligamande grade I sprain.

Exam Type: MRI KNEE LEFT WO CONTRAST
Exam Date and Time: [DATE] [TIME]
Indication: 3 months of atraumatic knee pain.
Comparison: [REDACTED].

TECHNIQUE:
MRI of the left knee was performed on a 1.5 Tesla system with a dedicated knee coil in three planes (axial, sagittal, and coronal), using a standard non-contrast protocol.

FINDINGS:
OSSEOUS STRUCTURES:
Alignment is anatomic. No acute fracture or bone bruise. Background marrow signal is normal without infiltrative marrow process. No aggressive osseous lesions.

JOINT SPACE:
Small joint effusion. No intra-articular bodies. Trace Baker's cyst.

MEDIAL COMPARTMENT:
Medial meniscus: Normal in morphology and signal.
Medial compartment cartilage: Focal high-grade partial thickness cartilage loss along the inner weightbearing aspect of the femoral condyle. Tibial cartilage is maintained.

LATERAL COMPARTMENT:
Lateral meniscus: Normal in morphology and signal.
Lateral compartment cartilage: No focal cartilage defects.

PATELLOFEMORAL COMPARTMENT:
Patellofemoral compartment cartilage: Partial-thickness thinning of the superolateral patellar cartilage with foci of high-grade fissuring. Trochlear cartilage is maintained.

CRUCIATE LIGAMENTS:
Anterior cruciate ligament (ACL): Normal with both bundles intact.
Posterior cruciate ligament (PCL): Normal.

COLLATERAL LIGAMENTS & POSTEROLATERAL CORNER:
Medial collateral ligament (MCL): Normal.
Lateral collateral ligament (LCL) complex: Normal.
Posterolateral corner structures: Normal.

EXTENSOR MECHANISM:
Distal quadriceps tendon: No tendinosis or tear.
Patella tendon: Mild proximal patellar tendinosis. No tendon tear.
Medial patellofemoral ligament (MPFL) and patellar retinacula: Normal.
Patellofemoral tracking: No edema in superolateral Hoffa's fat pad. No lateral patellar tilt or translation. No patella alta. Normal patellar and trochlear morphology. Normal tibial tubercle-trochlear groove (TT-TG) distance measuring 13 mm.

MUSCLES/TENDONS:
No acute muscle strain or muscle atrophy. Visualized tendons not previously discussed are intact without tendinosis or tear.

SOFT TISSUES:
No soft tissue mass. Normal popliteal neurovascular bundle.

IMPRESSION:
1.	No acute osseous or meniscal injury.
2.	Moderate medial and mild patellofemoral compartment chondrosis.
3.	Mild proximal patellar tendinosis.

Regelrechte Stellungs- und Artikulationsverhältnisse im linken Knie. Regelrechtes Knochenmarksignal ohne Hinweis auf einen Ödem. Kein Nachweis einer frischen Fraktur.
Bekannte fokale Chondropathie zentral und medial in der Trochlea (4/14). Regelrechter retropatellarer Knorpel. Unauffällige Darstellung des Hoffa'schen Fettkörpers.
Unauffällige Darstellung des medialen femorotibialen Gelenkes mit intaktem Innenmeniskus und mediales Kollateralband.
Konstante posttherapeutische Signalanhebungen des Außenmeniskus mit geringem Substanzdefekt im Vorderhorn. Suszeptibilitätsartefakte im lateralen femorotibialen Kompartiment, DD postop. (zB 3/107). Keine neue menisceale Rissbildung. Bekannter 3 mm messender nach oberflächlich reichender Knorpeldefekt der lateralen Femurkondyle (7/25). Konstante im Knorpelniveau gelegene Verknöcherung anstelle des vormals vordokumentierten vollschichtigen Knorpeldefektes (6/95 oder 7/25). Weiterhin kein Knochenmarködem nach Glättung des Knorpeldefektes an der lateralen Femurkondyle.
Kreuzbänder vollständig abgrenzbar. Laterales Kollateralband intakt. Akzentuierte Gelenksflüssigkeit.

Regelrechte Artikulation im linken Kniegelenk. Kleine Insertionszysten an der Eminentia und der linken Femurkondyle (5/21 und 5/18) mit Umgebend geringe Ödem. Ebenfalls kleine Geröllzysten und subkortikales Ödem in der medialen Femurkondyle und am medialen Tibiaplateau. Ansonsten unauffälliges Knochenmarkssignal.
Patella zentriert stehend. Mehrere mittelgradige chondrale Läsionen retropatellar, exemplarisch am First (4/12). Auch in der Trochlea mindestens mittelgradige Chondropathie (4/12). Femorotibial medialseitig am Hinterhorn deutlich substanzgemindert und extrudierter Restmeniskus (5/20) mit vollständig aufgebrauchter Knorpelschicht (5/20). Der Außenmeniskus im Vorderhorn deutlich signalangehoben (6/24). Lateralseitig in der Hauptbelastungszone ebenfalls ausgedünnter Knorpelbelag. 
Deutliche osteophytäre Anbauten am femoral und tibial sowie femoropatellar.
VKB und HKB intakt. LCL unauffällig. Angrenzend an das MCL schmaler Flüssigkeitssaum, DD bei Reizung. Gelenkerguss. Multiple villöse synoviale Proliferationen. Baker-Zyste. Unauffällige Darstellung der umgebenden Muskulatur und Subkutis.

Antecedentes Clínicos:
Rotura meniscal medial de rodilla izquierda
Hallazgos:
Ligamentos cruzados y colateral lateral sin alteraciones.
Aumento de señal del componente superficial del ligamento colateral medial sin signos de rotura.
Pérdida parcial de la continuidad de la inserción femoral del componente profundo menisco
femoral. El resto de los componentes del complejo medial sin alteraciones. Edema las partes
blandas regionales.
Edema óseo periférico del cóndilo femoral medial y del platillo tibial medial con pequeñas fracturas
subcorticales regionales.
Aumento de señal central del cuerno posterior del menisco medial que no contacta la superficie
articular, sin caracteres propios de rotura.
Úlceras condrales focales de espesor total de la zona de carga del cóndilo femoral medial en su
aspecto anterior. El resto de los cartílagos femorotibiales sin alteraciones.
Mínimo edema óseo periférico del cóndilo femoral lateral con pequeña fractura subcortical
regional.
Finas úlceras condrales de espesor parcial del aspecto inferior de la vertiente medial y región
central de la tróclea femoral. Cartílago rotuliano sin alteraciones.
Leve derrame articular. Quiste poplíteo con fenómenos de filtración hacia cefálico y caudal.
Cambios entesopáticos cuadricipitales distales. Tendón rotuliano, tendones de la pata de ganso,
bíceps femoral y banda iliotibial dentro de límites normales. Edema del las partes blandas siendo a
los tendones de la pata de ganso.
Impresión:
Signos de un esguince de bajo grado del componente superficial del ligamento colateral medial.
Signos de un esguince grado II del componente profundo menisco femoral en su inserción
femoral.
Edema óseo periférico del cóndilo femoral medial y medial con pequeñas fracturas subcorticales
regionales.
Condropatía con lesión focal grado 4 del aspecto anterior de la zona de carga del cóndilo femoral
medial.
Mínimo edema óseo periférico del cóndilo femoral lateral con pequeña fractura subcortical
regional.
Condropatía con lesiones grado 2 de la tróclea femoral.
Leve derrame articular. Quiste poplíteo o fenómenos de filtración.
Cambios entesopáticos cuadricipitales distales

FINDINGS:

Fluid:
Moderate joint effusion. Large Baker's cyst measuring up to 6.3 cm with associated fluid inferiorly along the medial gastrocnemius suggesting a partial leak.

Medial compartment (meniscus, collateral ligament, cartilage):
There is a mildly complex tear of the posterior horn and body of the medial meniscus extending to the anterior horn with a longitudinal horizontal and radial components and a flap meniscal tear probably originating from the posterior horn, displaced posteriorly and superiorly at the level of the posterior horn posterior root junction. There is also a second flap meniscal tear at the level of the superior gutter at the medial tibiofemoral joint line with a displaced flap anterosuperiorly. Please see key images. There is some radial tearing at the level of the posterior root. There is significant extrusion of the meniscal body/anterior horn junction with maceration.

There is thickening of the medial collateral ligament at the level of the superficial and deep meniscal femoral fibers consistent with a grade 1 sprain.

There is severe degenerative changes/chondropathy at the medial tibiofemoral compartment with full-thickness chondral fissures and subchondral bone marrow reactive changes, notably at the medial aspect of the weightbearing surfaces.

Lateral compartment (meniscus, collateral ligament complex, cartilage):
The lateral meniscus and lateral collateral ligament complex are intact without tear.

There is mild to moderate diffuse chondral thinning at the lateral tibiofemoral compartment consistent with chondropathy/degenerative changes.

Intercondylar compartment (anterior and posterior cruciate ligaments):
Normal. Para ligament ganglion cysts. Underlying intraosseous ganglion cysts.

Anterior compartment (extensor mechanism, cartilage, Hoffa's fat pad):
The patellofemoral alignment is within normal limits. Mild distal quadricep and moderate patellar tendinosis notably at the proximal aspect without definite tear. There is likely reactive bone marrow edema at the inferior pole of the patella at the origin of the patellar tendon.

There is moderate to severe chondral thinning at the patellofemoral compartment with full-thickness chondral loss at the level of the trochlea and subchondral bone marrow reactive changes.

Bones:
Normal otherwise.

Muscles and neurovascular structures:
Normal.

Other findings:
None

CONCLUSION:
Potentially unstable complex medial meniscal tear with longitudinal and radial components and flap meniscal tears with displaced flap posteriorly and superiorly at the level of the posterior horn posterior root junction and anterosuperiorly at the level of the superior gutter at the medial tibiofemoral joint line. Please see key images.

Tricompartmental degenerative changes/chondropathy, severe at the medial tibiofemoral compartment and moderate to severe at the patellofemoral compartment as detailed above.

Moderate joint effusion. Large Baker's cyst with signs of partial leak.

Other findings as detailed above.

Findings:  Moderately sized joint effusion. No intra-articular loose bodies. No sinister bone marrow changes.  Intact cruciate and collateral ligaments. Intact lateral meniscus.  Degenerate tearing/maceration of the body and posterior horn of the medial meniscus.  Normal appearance of the distal biceps femoris tendon, distal iliotibial band, pes anserine tendons and popliteus tendon.  Intact quadriceps and patellar tendons. Borderline patella alta. The patella is lateralized relative to the femoral trochlear groove. 
Evidence of trochlear dysplasia with a shallow trochlear groove and borderline reduced lateral trochlear inclination. Normal TTâ€“TG. The MPFL and medial patellar retinaculum are intact.  High-grade chondral thinning centered along the median patellar ridge with underlying bone stress change. Focal high-grade chondral thinning is also demonstrated in the weightbearing portion of the medial femoral condyle. Relatively well-maintained hyaline articular cartilage in the lateral tibiofemoral compartment. Small tricompartmental marginal osteophyte formation.  
Conclusion:  Evidence of trochlear dysplasia with features of patellofemoral instability. Degenerative changes in the patellofemoral and medial tibiofemoral compartments as described. Degenerate tearing/maceration of the body and posterior horn of the medial meniscus.
